$comment: Canned replies for the stand-in platform (demo/fake-platform.js in the case desk engine), so this desk can be tried with no platform. Each key is a distinctive part of a case title, matched without regard to case. The stand-in adds its own first line saying that the reply is canned. The replies follow the right answers in demo-bank/SCENARIOS.md. An alert reply carries a narrative under its own heading. The place of an article is given in words with its id, because a stand-in has no real address to give; a real agent gives the page address the bank returns. The bank, its customers and its press archive are invented. Start the stand-in with DESK_CONFIG pointing at desk.config.json in this folder.

replies.Brightwater:
Summary
Brightwater Cash and Carry Ltd (CUS-1020), a cash-and-carry grocer, account ACC-1020-01. Rule MTB-AML-RULE-001 fired on alert TMA-3001, risk score 86.
Seven cash deposits of USD 9,100 to 9,800 (TXN-S3001-01 to TXN-S3001-07) were made in 10 days, total USD 66,450, each under the USD 10,000 reporting threshold. Earlier deposits were USD 1,400 to 3,100.
A branch note, CNT-5008, says the owner now brings deposits in batches. No business reason is on record.
Saved: not saved. This reply comes from the stand-in, not from the monitoring system. A real run saves the findings and the narrative on alert TMA-3001 as a draft.

Draft case file. For the investigator. Not decided.

| # | Finding | Evidence | What it shows | Found at | Mark | What to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Seven cash deposits just under USD 10,000 | TXN-S3001-01 to TXN-S3001-07 | USD 9,400, 9,650, 9,100, 9,800, 9,300, 9,700 and 9,500, total USD 66,450 | The account's transactions | supports concern | Each is under the reporting threshold. The investigator should check whether the cash fits the customer's trade and takings. |
| 2 | Earlier cash deposits were much smaller | TXN-102001-0001 to TXN-102001-0004 | USD 1,850, 2,200, 1,400 and 3,100 | The account's transactions | supports concern | The size of the deposits changed sharply. Check what changed in the business. |
| 3 | The rule's own conditions are met | MTB-AML-RULE-001; TMA-3001 | Three or more deposits between USD 9,000 and 9,999 within 14 days, or USD 30,000 or more just under the threshold | The monitoring rule | supports concern | All seven deposits are between USD 9,100 and 9,800. The rule describes a pattern known as structuring. The records show the pattern. They do not show intent. |
| 4 | The owner now brings deposits in batches | CNT-5008 | Branch note: the owner brings deposits in batches to keep things tidy, several in the last two weeks | The customer's contact history | supports concern | The note records the practice and gives no business reason. Ask the branch what the owner said. |
| 5 | Payments out to a supplier | TXN-102001-0005 to TXN-102001-0007 | USD 8,200, 12,100 and 11,800 to Alder and Vine Wholesale, supplier payments | The account's transactions | neutral | An ordinary supplier for a grocer. The three payments total USD 32,100 against USD 66,450 of deposits. |
| 6 | An earlier alert on the same rule | TMA-2901 | Two deposits just under the threshold, closed with no further action: single event, a market day | The customer's alert history | neutral | The earlier alert had two deposits, and this one has seven. The earlier closure does not speak to these deposits. |
| 7 | No press coverage found for Brightwater Cash and Carry | none | A search of the press archive for "Brightwater Cash and Carry" returned no article. | The press archive | missing | Nothing found is not a finding either way. |

Investigation narrative. Draft. Not decided.

Brightwater Cash and Carry Ltd (CUS-1020) is a cash-and-carry grocer in Tallowby. Alert TMA-3001 was raised on its account ACC-1020-01 under rule MTB-AML-RULE-001, which looks for cash deposits just under the USD 10,000 reporting threshold. The alert's risk score is 86.

Seven cash deposits were made in 10 days (TXN-S3001-01 to TXN-S3001-07): USD 9,400, 9,650, 9,100, 9,800, 9,300, 9,700 and 9,500. They total USD 66,450. Each is under the USD 10,000 reporting threshold and inside the rule's band of USD 9,000 to 9,999. The records fit the pattern the rule describes. They do not show why the deposits are of this size.

Before these, the account's cash deposits were USD 1,850, 2,200, 1,400 and 3,100 (TXN-102001-0001 to TXN-102001-0004). Every deposit in the alert is larger than any of them. Three payments to a supplier, Alder and Vine Wholesale, went out over a similar period (TXN-102001-0005 to TXN-102001-0007): USD 8,200, 12,100 and 11,800, total USD 32,100, which is less than half of the USD 66,450 deposited.

A branch note, CNT-5008, records that the owner now brings deposits in batches "to keep things tidy", several in the last two weeks. The note records the practice and gives no business reason for splitting the deposits. The same rule fired once before on this customer, alert TMA-2901, with two deposits. It was closed with no further action as a single event, a market day. That closure does not speak to these seven deposits.

The press archive holds no article about Brightwater Cash and Carry. Nothing found is not a finding either way.

What is missing: a business reason for the batches, and any figure for the shop's takings. The branch could say what the owner told the cashier.

Recommendation: open a case. Seven cash deposits just under the reporting threshold, after months of much smaller ones, fit the pattern the rule describes, and the records give no business reason for the batches. The alert's risk score is 86. The investigator decides.

Investigation narrative. Draft. Not decided.

Nimbus Transit Consulting Ltd (CUS-1021) is a transport consultancy at Cinder Quay. Alert TMA-3002 was raised on its account ACC-1021-01 under rule MTB-AML-RULE-002, which looks for a credit of USD 25,000 or more that leaves within two business days with at least 90 percent of the amount, three times in 30 days. The alert's risk score is 82.

Three credits came in from Tallowmere Holdings (CPY-4001): USD 48,000, 52,500 and 39,000 (TXN-S3002-1A, TXN-S3002-2A and TXN-S3002-3A), described as a consulting fee. Each left the next day to Quillgate Trading (CPY-4002) as USD 47,400, 51,800 and 38,400 (TXN-S3002-1B, TXN-S3002-2B and TXN-S3002-3B), described as services. In all, USD 139,500 came in and USD 137,600 went out, so USD 1,900 stayed, about 1.36 percent. Each round kept 1.25, 1.33 and 1.54 percent. The records fit the pattern the rule describes.

Tallowmere Holdings (CPY-4001) is recorded as a holding company in Aldoria, rated medium risk, with no public information on its trade. Quillgate Trading (CPY-4002) is recorded in Brevnia, rated medium risk, and receives large transfers from several unrelated senders. The records state these facts and no more.

A call note, CNT-5009, says the customer uses the account for client fees and could not name the clients paying large sums. The call took place before the first of the three credits. The customer has no earlier alert and no case. The press archive holds nothing about the customer or either counterparty.

What is missing: a contract or an invoice for the consulting fees, the names of the clients, and any reason a holding company pays a consultancy this much. The customer could supply these. Nothing on record explains why each credit left the next day.

Recommendation: open a case. Three large credits from one sender each left the next day to another party, keeping about 1.36 percent, and the customer could not name its clients. The records fit the pattern the rule describes. The investigator decides.

Copperfield Import Traders Ltd (CUS-1022) is an import and trading business at Dock Road, rated medium risk. Alert TMA-3003 was raised on its account ACC-1022-01 under rule MTB-AML-RULE-003, which looks for payments to counterparties in a country on the bank's higher-risk list totalling USD 20,000 or more in 30 days. Kharnovia is on that list. The alert's risk score is 74.

Four payments went to Karn Harbour Freight Agency (CPY-4005) in Kharnovia (TXN-S3003-1 to TXN-S3003-4): USD 14,800, 9,950, 12,300 and 16,200, described as freight and handling. They total USD 53,250 in 24 days, over the rule's USD 20,000. That is the rule's trigger and it is not wrongdoing by itself.

The agency is a new counterparty, first seen 24 days ago, rated high risk, with no contract on file. The customer told the bank in an email, CNT-5010, that it had begun using a freight agent in Kharnovia, and sent no contract. The email is dated before the first payment. A freight agent is a plausible need for an import business.

Two articles are about the agency, and both name Gallowmere, Kharnovia, as the counterparty record does. ART-6003 reports a customs inquiry over containers declared as machine parts. ART-6004 reports an accusation by a trade monitoring group that the agency moved goods for buyers on a sanctions list, and says the agency did not answer. Both report an inquiry or an accusation, not a finding.

The customer has no earlier alert and no case.

What is missing: the freight contract and the invoices behind each of the four payments. The customer could supply them, and could say whether the payments relate to the shipments named in the articles. Nothing here is proven.

Recommendation: open a case at medium priority. The payments are to a new counterparty in a higher-risk country with press coverage of an inquiry, and no contract or invoice is on record. The customer's trade plausibly needs freight, so nothing here is proven. Ask for the contract and the invoices. The investigator decides.

Summary
Saltmarsh Catering Co (CUS-1023), a festival and event caterer, account ACC-1023-01. Rule MTB-AML-RULE-004 fired on alert TMA-3004, risk score 52.
The alert counts 41 outgoing payroll payments this month against an average of 22 (TXN-S3004-01 to TXN-S3004-41). The 22 regular payees and their amounts are unchanged, and 19 extra payments are seasonal payroll.
The owner said in a call, CNT-5011, that about twenty seasonal staff would be hired. A festival contract advance of USD 98,000 arrived the day before, and a news article, ART-6014, says the customer is hiring.
Saved: not saved. This reply comes from the stand-in, not from the monitoring system. A real run saves the findings and the narrative on alert TMA-3004 as a draft.

Draft case file. For the investigator. Not decided.

| # | Finding | Evidence | What it shows | Found at | Mark | What to check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Payroll payments rose from 22 to 41 | TMA-3004; MTB-AML-RULE-004 | 41 outgoing payroll payments in the month against an average of 22 | The monitoring alert | neutral | The rule fires at 1.5 times the average. This is what raised the alert, and a rise in payroll is not wrongdoing by itself. |
| 2 | The 22 regular payees are unchanged | TXN-S3004-01 to TXN-S3004-22; TXN-102301-0001 to TXN-102301-0044 | The same 22 named payees and the same amounts, USD 1,850 to 2,450, as in the two earlier months | The account's transactions | explains the activity | The extra payments are in addition to the regular payroll. The regular payroll did not change. |
| 3 | Nineteen extra payees are seasonal staff | TXN-S3004-23 to TXN-S3004-41 | 19 payments described as seasonal payroll, USD 1,500 to 1,770 | The account's transactions | explains the activity | 19 plus 22 is 41. Check the seasonal staff against the customer's hiring records if the investigator wants more. |
| 4 | The owner said seasonal staff would be hired | CNT-5011 | Call note: about twenty seasonal staff will be hired for the harvest festival season, and payroll will be larger for a few weeks | The customer's contact history | explains the activity | The customer told the bank about it before it happened. |
| 5 | A contract advance arrived the day before | TXN-102301-0045 | USD 98,000 from Foxfield Hospitality, a festival catering contract advance | The account's transactions | explains the activity | The advance matches a festival contract. The contract itself is not on record that the agent can read. |
| 6 | Public news of the festival contract and the hiring | ART-6014 | Saltmarsh Catering Co has won the contract to feed visitors at the harvest festival and is hiring about twenty seasonal staff | The press archive, article ART-6014 | explains the activity | The article names the customer, its town and its trade. |
| 7 | An earlier alert on the same rule | TMA-2902 | Payment count above average, closed with no further action: summer event staff | The customer's alert history | explains the activity | The earlier closure is context and not proof for this month. |

Investigation narrative. Draft. Not decided.

Saltmarsh Catering Co (CUS-1023) is a festival and event caterer in Marlow Reach. Alert TMA-3004 was raised on its account ACC-1023-01 under rule MTB-AML-RULE-004, which fires when the count of outgoing payments in a month is 1.5 times the three-month average or more. The alert counts 41 outgoing payroll payments this month against an average of 22. The alert's risk score is 52.

The 22 regular payees (TXN-S3004-01 to TXN-S3004-22) were paid the same amounts, USD 1,850 to 2,450, as in the two earlier months (TXN-102301-0001 to TXN-102301-0044). The other 19 payments (TXN-S3004-23 to TXN-S3004-41) are described as seasonal payroll, USD 1,500 to 1,770 each. 22 and 19 make 41.

The owner told the bank in a call, CNT-5011, that about twenty seasonal staff would be hired for the harvest festival season and that payroll would be larger for a few weeks. The call was made before the hiring. A credit of USD 98,000 from Foxfield Hospitality (TXN-102301-0045), described as a festival catering contract advance, arrived the day before the payroll.

A news article, ART-6014, says Saltmarsh Catering Co of Marlow Reach has won the contract to feed visitors at the harvest festival and is hiring about twenty seasonal staff. It names the customer, its town and its trade. An earlier alert on the same rule, TMA-2902, was closed with no further action as summer event staff. That closure is context and not proof for this month.

What is missing: the festival contract itself is not on record where the agent could read it. The records give an innocent reading of the alert, and the regular payroll did not change.

Recommendation: no case. The extra payroll payments are the 19 seasonal staff the owner described in advance, the regular payroll is unchanged, and a festival contract advance and a news article support it. The investigator decides whether to close the alert.
